facts.text: Port Vincent was founded by Italian merchant Vincent Scivicque, who donated land for a cemetery in 1824 and built a chapel blessed in 1839.
Originally called Subique’s Ferry, the town became a vital Amite River shipping point for Spanish traders until 1814 when Andrew Jackson dammed the Mississippi entrance to Bayou Manchac.
Port Vincent briefly served as the Livingston Parish seat from 1872 to 1881, but its courthouse burned in 1875, destroying public records.
The historic Port Vincent Bridge over the Amite River was renovated, preserving a key piece of the town’s transportation heritage.
Port Vincent lies on the Amite River, which forms the boundary between Livingston and Ascension parishes.
The town’s proximity to Baton Rouge—about 25 miles—has shifted its economy from river shipping to a suburban and recreational character.
